tools.name: Oracle Data Integrator
tools.stack: ODI 14c agents + Knowledge Modules; GoldenGate JKM only for proven S0/S1 feeds; Automic calls ODI scenarios / load plans
tools.licensing: Per processor or Named User Plus on every host running an ODI agent (list ref. USD 30k/processor + 22% annual support). WebLogic EE + Coherence EE needed for clustered agent HA. GoldenGate licensed separately on capture/delivery hosts.
tools.lifecycle: FMW 14.1.2 Premier Support to Dec 2030, Extended to Dec 2033. ODI 12c Premier ends Dec 2026, Extended Dec 2027. Next FMW release targeted 2027.
strengths: Generates set-based SQL that runs inside Exadata (Smart Scan, HCC, parallel DML, partition exchange) - no second compute tier
Knowledge Modules for SCD2, incremental merge, CDC and bulk load (external tables, SQL*Loader, DB link from standby)
Native GoldenGate journalizing (JKM) when a data product truly needs S0/S1
Repository-based lineage and impact analysis; load plans with restart from failure point
Already in the Turkish capital-markets ecosystem (Borsa Istanbul uses ODI); local partners exist
weaknesses: GUI-centric development; Git integration exists but merge/branching is awkward compared to code-first tools
Licence follows agent hosts; HA topology adds WebLogic/Coherence licences
Real-time capability is borrowed from GoldenGate, which the DBA team distrusts and has no 24/7 cover for
14c requires Python 3 for custom KMs (Jython deprecated) - small learning item
tools.fit: Best structural fit: Oracle-only estate, Exadata already paid for, PL/SQL team, Kale-centric sources, files and BIDB pulls.

tools.name: Informatica PowerCenter
tools.stack: PowerCenter Integration Service + Repository; PowerExchange CDC for Oracle (separate licence); Pushdown Optimization option
tools.licensing: Quote-based; on-prem PowerCenter no longer sold to new customers per the Informatica partner (BI Technology) - successor CDI-PC is IPU consumption-based via an internet-connected IDMC Secure Agent.
tools.lifecycle: Standard support ended 31 Mar 2026. Paid Extended Support to 31 Mar 2027, Sustaining Support (no new fixes / security patches) to 31 Mar 2029. Informatica acquired by Salesforce (Nov 2025).
strengths: Very broad connectivity (files, FTP, web services, mainframe, all major RDBMS)
Mature workflow manager, restartability and operational monitoring
Metadata Manager lineage; large pool of PowerCenter developers in Turkey (MKK uses it)
Takasbank already has an Informatica relationship (TDM for non-prod masking)
weaknesses: End-of-support product: buying it in 2026 for a 10-year DWH is buying a forced migration
Successor (CDI-PC / IDMC) puts the control plane in the cloud - conflicts with 'data and operations stay inside the bank'
Row-by-row engine by default; full pushdown to Exadata needs the PDO option and still leaves an ETL server tier
Repository-based development; weak Git/CI story
tools.fit: Fails the support-horizon gate. Only defensible as a short-term bridge for an existing PowerCenter estate - which Takasbank does not have.

tools.name: dbt (dbt-core + dbt-oracle)
tools.version: dbt-core 1.12 + dbt-oracle 1.12 (dbt v2/Fusion has no Oracle adapter yet)
tools.stack: dbt-core + dbt-oracle on Linux runners; ingestion by PL/SQL + external tables/SQL*Loader (or ODI); Automic runs `dbt build`; Git + CI
tools.licensing: Apache 2.0, no licence fee. dbt platform (SaaS) is not usable on-prem; no vendor SLA for self-hosted Core. Fivetran + dbt Labs merger completed 1 Jun 2026.
tools.lifecycle: Minor releases roughly quarterly, one year of support each (1.12 critical support to Jul 2027). dbt-oracle maintained by Oracle; v2 parser does not recognise Oracle yet.
strengths: Pure SQL pushdown on Exadata - same compute advantage as ODI
Code-first: Git, pull-request review, automated tests, environments, docs site
Built-in data tests, snapshots (SCD2), incremental merge and microbatch strategies
Zero licence cost and no procurement - can start the pilot immediately
weaknesses: Transformation only: no extraction, file handling, web services or CDC - a landing framework must be built
Model-level lineage only in Core; column-level lineage is a dbt platform (SaaS) feature
No commercial support for on-prem Core; Oracle adapter lags the cloud-warehouse adapters
Jinja/YAML and Git workflow are new to a PL/SQL team
tools.fit: Strong transformation layer and the fastest start, but needs a separate, home-built ingestion and orchestration layer.

tools.name: Cloudera Data Platform (Base on premises)
tools.version: Cloudera Base on premises 7.3.2 LTS + Cloudera Streaming (Kafka, Flink) + Flow Management (NiFi)
tools.stack: Cloudera Base cluster (Ozone/HDFS, Iceberg, Hive/Impala, Spark), Cloudera Streaming (Kafka/Flink, Kafka Connect + Debezium), NiFi for files/web services, Atlas/Ranger (SDX)
tools.licensing: Subscription by Cloudera Compute Units (cores/6 + RAM GB/12) plus Data Under Management since Feb 2025; quote-based. Requires its own commodity-server cluster - cannot run on Exadata.
tools.lifecycle: 7.3.2 LTS GA Mar 2026, supported to Mar 2032. 7.3.1 EoS Dec 2026, 7.1.9 Oct 2028.
strengths: Strongest native streaming stack (Kafka, Flink, NiFi) for S0 event pipelines
SDX governance: Atlas lineage, Ranger policies, Kerberos - fully on-prem
NiFi handles FTP/CSV, EPIAS web services and API ingestion well
Scales to data sizes far beyond Takasbank's (~10 TB Kale)
weaknesses: A second data platform beside three Exadata machines that are 77-90% free
Data must leave Exadata to be processed and come back for MSTR - double copies, double security perimeter
Hadoop/Kafka/Spark skills absent; needs a platform team and 24/7 operations
Oracle CDC still needs a log reader (Debezium LogMiner or GoldenGate) on the Kale side
tools.fit: Over-sized for a 10 TB Oracle-centric DWH. Revisit only for a future streaming/AI or unstructured-data mandate.

tools.name: Apache Spark (self-managed)
tools.stack: Spark 4.2 (SQL, Structured Streaming, Declarative Pipelines) + Kafka + Debezium + Airflow/Automic + Iceberg or JDBC write-back to Oracle; DIY security and lineage (OpenLineage)
tools.licensing: Apache 2.0, no licence fee. No vendor support unless bought from a third party.
tools.lifecycle: Feature release roughly every 6-7 months (4.0 May 2025, 4.1 Dec 2025, 4.2 Jul 2026); maintenance releases for a limited window per line.
strengths: Most flexible engine: Python/Scala/SQL, ML, streaming (Real-time Mode), CDC APIs in 4.2
No licence cost; huge community
Code-first, testable, Git-native
weaknesses: Everything around the engine is DIY: scheduling, security, lineage, monitoring, upgrades
Moves data off Exadata through JDBC - the slowest path for a 2-billion-row SWIFT table
Requires Python/Scala data engineers and a platform team Takasbank does not have
Real-time Mode is still marked experimental for parts of the API
tools.fit: Weakest fit: maximum engineering load, minimum use of existing Oracle investment.

criteria.name: Exadata / Oracle pushdown and performance
criteria.what: Runs set-based work inside Exadata (Smart Scan, HCC, parallel DML), handles 2B-row SWIFT and 20M/day takas volumes without a second compute tier.

criteria.name: Real-time, CDC and operational reporting
criteria.what: Supports S0 near-real-time and S1 micro-batch for izleme screens and intraday Fon Bilgilendirme without touching prod Kale.

criteria.name: Security, on-prem and regulatory compliance
criteria.what: Fully on-prem with no external control plane; BDDK/KVKK/SPK fit; TDE/VPD/redaction respected; security patches through the horizon.

criteria.name: Governance: lineage, metadata, audit, data quality
criteria.what: Column-level source-to-report lineage, run lineage, audit trail and data-quality rules for regulatory reports.

criteria.name: Team skill fit and learning curve
criteria.what: Usable by an Oracle DBA / PL/SQL team with no DWH/ETL background; hiring market in Turkey.

criteria.name: Source connectivity
criteria.what: Kale standby, ARSIV, CekDB, BIST Replica BIDB / Borsa DWH, FTP/CSV, EPIAS web services, possible Postgres/MSSQL.

criteria.name: Transformation and modelling
criteria.what: SCD2, bitemporal core, incremental merge, set-based logic, reuse of existing PL/SQL.

criteria.name: 5-year total cost of ownership
criteria.what: Licence + support + infrastructure + people over five years (higher score = lower cost).

criteria.name: Operations and orchestration
criteria.what: Automic integration, gün sonu event triggering, restart from failure, monitoring, without a 24/7 team.

criteria.name: DevOps: Git, CI/CD, automated tests
criteria.what: Version control, code review, automated tests and promotion DEV -> TEST -> PREPROD -> PROD.

criteria.name: Vendor viability, roadmap and local support
criteria.what: Supported release horizon, roadmap risk, ownership changes, partners in Turkey.

pushdown.why: E-LT by design: generated SQL runs in the target Exadata; Oracle KMs use external tables, parallel DML, MERGE and partition exchange.

realtime.why: Batch and micro-batch natively; S0 only via GoldenGate JKM (separate licence, DBA concerns). ADG standby covers raw izleme screens.

security.why: Fully on-prem; agents run inside the bank; credentials in the ODI repository/wallet; relies on Oracle DB security (TDE, VPD).

governance.why: Repository holds mappings, column lineage and impact analysis; run history per session. DQ needs custom checks or Oracle EDQ.

skills.why: SQL-centric; PL/SQL developers become productive quickly. GUI and KM concepts need training.

connectivity.why: Oracle, JDBC (Postgres/MSSQL), files, FTP, web-service tools; BIDB pull from Borsa DWH as Ondata described.

transform.why: Built-in SCD2 and incremental IKMs; bitemporal patterns via custom KM; existing procedure SQL reusable.

tco.why: Processor licences on agent hosts plus 22% annual support; HA adds WebLogic/Coherence. No extra compute (Exadata).

operations.why: Load plans with restart, agent HA, Automic triggers scenarios via command line or web service.

devops.why: VCS/Git integration and deployment archives exist, but branching and merging repository objects is clumsy.

vendor.why: Oracle; 14c supported to 2030/2033; Borsa Istanbul reference; local integrators.

pushdown.why: Engine-based ETL; Pushdown Optimization (extra option) can push to Oracle, but an ETL server tier remains.

realtime.why: PowerExchange CDC for Oracle (separate licence) gives log-based capture; real-time option exists.

security.why: On-prem today, but security fixes stop after Extended Support (Mar 2027); successor needs an internet-connected Secure Agent and cloud control plane.

governance.why: Metadata Manager lineage and mature audit; DQ via separate Informatica products.

skills.why: No in-house ETL skills; PowerCenter developers available in the Turkish market (MKK).

connectivity.why: Broadest connector catalogue of the five: files, FTP, web services, all RDBMS, mainframe.

transform.why: Rich transformation library, SCD wizards, lookups; logic lives in the engine, not in SQL.

tco.why: Quote-based licence, extended-support premium, and a forced migration to IDMC within the 5-year window.

operations.why: Workflow Manager/Monitor, restart and recovery are mature.

devops.why: Repository-centric; XML export for Git; weak CI/CD.

vendor.why: On-prem product at end of standard support; now part of Salesforce; partner reported no new on-prem sales.

pushdown.why: Every model compiles to SQL executed in Exadata; incremental merge and microbatch strategies supported by dbt-oracle.

realtime.why: No CDC or streaming; microbatch runs give S1 at best; S0 must come from ADG or GoldenGate.

security.why: Self-hosted Core sends no data out; runs with DB accounts; secrets handled by the runner. Do not use dbt platform (SaaS).

governance.why: DAG lineage, docs site and built-in tests; column-level lineage only in the SaaS platform; run artifacts must be harvested.

skills.why: SQL first; Jinja macros, YAML and Git are new but small steps for SQL people.

connectivity.why: None: dbt only transforms what is already in the database; landing must be built separately.

transform.why: Snapshots (SCD2), incremental models, tests, macros; bitemporal handled with custom macros.

tco.why: No licence; people cost for building the ingestion/orchestration framework.

operations.why: CLI runs from Automic; `dbt retry` for restarts; monitoring built from run_results artifacts.

devops.why: Best-in-class: Git, pull requests, CI, environment targets, slim CI.

vendor.why: Open source with no on-prem SLA; Oracle adapter community/Oracle-maintained and not yet on v2 engine; vendor focus is cloud.

pushdown.why: Processing happens on the Cloudera cluster; Oracle is reached via JDBC/Sqoop-style pulls and results written back for MSTR.

realtime.why: Kafka + Flink + NiFi give true streaming; Oracle CDC still needs Debezium/LogMiner or GoldenGate on Kale side.

security.why: On-prem with Kerberos, Ranger, TLS; larger attack surface and second security perimeter.

governance.why: Atlas lineage and Ranger audit across the cluster; lineage breaks at the Oracle boundary.

skills.why: Hadoop, Kafka, Flink, Spark, Kerberos skills absent; scarce and expensive hires.

connectivity.why: NiFi plus Kafka Connect cover files, FTP, web services, APIs and all databases.

transform.why: Spark SQL / Hive / Iceberg MERGE are capable, but the integrated core would be split between two platforms.

tco.why: CCU + data-under-management subscription, a new server cluster, and a platform team on top of Exadata.

operations.why: Cloudera Manager helps, but a multi-service cluster needs 24/7 operations Takasbank lacks.

devops.why: Code-based jobs are Git-friendly; platform configuration is not.

vendor.why: 7.3.2 LTS supported to 2032; established vendor with Turkish banking references.

pushdown.why: Reads and writes Oracle through JDBC; no use of Smart Scan; 2B-row SWIFT reload is the worst case.

realtime.why: Structured Streaming and 4.x Real-time Mode with Kafka + Debezium; parts still experimental.

security.why: Everything (Kerberos/TLS, secrets, authorisation) is self-built and self-patched.

governance.why: Lineage via OpenLineage/DIY; no built-in catalogue or audit.

skills.why: Python/Scala distributed-systems engineering; furthest from the PL/SQL team.

connectivity.why: JDBC and files are fine; FTP/web services need custom code.

transform.why: Unlimited logic, but core tables live in Oracle, so every load is a cross-system write.

tco.why: No licence, but cluster hardware plus 3-5 platform/data engineers.

vendor.why: Community project; support only via third parties; fast release cadence to track.

latency.name: Near real-time (seconds)
latency.example: Izleme screens, Team Developer current-state queries
latency.recommended: Kale ADG read-only standby on sur; GoldenGate -> LND -> ODS_ projection only for products with a proven SLA

latency.name: Intraday micro-batch (5-30 min)
latency.recommended: Watermark/SCN-based micro-batch from the standby into LND, recompute affected funds only

odi.note: Scheduled load plans, CDC on watermark or GG

latency.name: Gün sonu (T-1)
latency.example: BISTECH SPK 13 reports, SWIFT legal reports, takas positions
latency.recommended: SCN-consistent extract from standby after the machine-readable gün sonu event

latency.name: Scheduled file / external feed
latency.example: FTP/CSV, EPIAS web services, Borsa DWH fund contracts, Verda file output
latency.recommended: Manifest + checksum landing; external tables for files; web-service pull into LND_FILE / LND_EPIAS

latency.name: Backfill / replay
latency.example: 10-year fund history, 2013+ SWIFT history, ARSIV yearly rollovers
latency.recommended: Replay from immutable landing with a separate load_id; partition exchange for bulk history

useCases.name: SWIFT legal reports
useCases.detail: 2B rows / 170 GB since 2013, ~1M messages/day; collapse to ~24M one-row-per-message summary; free-text ID search; T-1.

useCases.name: Fon Bilgilendirme platform
useCases.detail: ~60k fund notifications/day, recalculation 08:00-17:45 with correction files; 10-year history via CSV and web service.

useCases.name: Fon islem defterleri
useCases.detail: 9M Borsa DWH fund contracts/day (deleted at source after 5 days), cleanse to ~600k, files twice a day per market to Borsa Verda.

useCases.name: BISTECH SPK 13 reports
useCases.detail: Kale NOMX + Replica BIDB, after Takas UG gün sonu; replace DB_ARSIV dblink views with PUB snapshots.

useCases.name: EPIAS energy settlement feeds
useCases.detail: Order/settlement files via web services, 5-10k records/day, collateral data, avans.takas table.

useCases.name: Operational izleme screens (S0)
useCases.detail: Intraday current-state queries now hitting prod Kale from Team Developer / React.

useCases.name: Takas positions and history
useCases.detail: ~20M derivative and non-derivative positions/day; yearly banka -> banka_old -> arsiv rollover moves into DWH partitions.

tco.pwc: High: quote-based; extended-support premium; migration to IPU billing within window

tco.odi: GoldenGate per processor on capture/delivery hosts, only for S0 products (licence includes ADG entitlement)
tco.cdp: Included in Cloudera Streaming subscription; Oracle log reader still needed

tco.odi: Low: 2 agent VMs; compute on existing Exadata
tco.dbt: Low: runner VMs; compute on existing Exadata
tco.cdp: High: new multi-node cluster (storage, masters, Kafka brokers)

tco.dbt: 2-3 data engineers (incl. ingestion framework) + DevOps support

tco.odi: Medium: logic in KMs/mappings, SQL is visible

risks.risk: GoldenGate operational burden if S0 products are approved
risks.mitigation: Serve raw izleme from ADG standby first; GoldenGate only per product with DBA on-call agreed; monitor lag in CTL.

risks.risk: Licence scope creep (agents on more hosts, HA needs WebLogic EE)
risks.mitigation: Fix agent topology before the PO; standalone agents with Automic-level failover instead of WebLogic cluster.

risks.risk: GUI development hides logic from code review
risks.mitigation: ODI VCS on Git, naming standards, scenario versioning, generated-SQL review in PR.

risks.risk: Product end-of-life forces a second migration
risks.mitigation: Do not select; if ever considered, price the IDMC migration and confirm on-prem control-plane options in writing.

risks.risk: Cloud control plane conflicts with data-residency rules
risks.mitigation: Legal/compliance review of CDI-PC Secure Agent connectivity before any further evaluation.

risks.risk: Home-built ingestion framework becomes an unsupported product
risks.mitigation: Keep landing minimal (external tables, PL/SQL pulls from standby), documented and owned; or pair with ODI for ingestion.

risks.risk: Oracle adapter lags dbt v2 / Fusion
risks.mitigation: Pin dbt-core 1.x + dbt-oracle; track adapter roadmap; avoid features exclusive to the SaaS platform.

risks.risk: No vendor SLA for production incidents
risks.mitigation: Third-party support contract or internal runbooks; failure surface is small because SQL runs in Oracle.

risks.risk: Second platform without a platform team
risks.mitigation: Do not adopt for the core DWH; reconsider only with a funded streaming/AI programme and team.

risks.risk: Two copies of regulated data and two security perimeters
risks.mitigation: Ranger/Atlas + KVKK classification on both sides; avoid by keeping the DWH on Exadata.

risks.risk: DIY platform with no vendor support
risks.mitigation: Not recommended; if needed, buy commercial support and limit to non-critical analytics.

risks.risk: JDBC bottleneck for large Oracle loads
risks.mitigation: Partitioned parallel reads, or keep heavy SQL inside Exadata.

risks.risk: No machine-readable gün sonu completion signal
risks.mitigation: Batch-control record (business date, run id, SCN) produced by operations before any S2 pipeline goes live.

risks.risk: Historical rows updated in place break incremental loads
risks.mitigation: Profile change columns on the standby; fall back to SCN snapshots and hash-diff where no reliable timestamp exists.

poc.name: SWIFT bulk + delta
poc.measure: Initial load of the 2B-row history and daily delta into the summary table; elapsed time, Exadata CPU/IO, Smart Scan offload ratio.
poc.accept: Daily delta finishes inside the T-1 window; result matches the current Kale query for a sampled set of IDs.

poc.name: Intraday Fon recompute
poc.measure: Micro-batch from standby every 15 min, with a correction file mid-day.
poc.accept: End-to-end freshness 15 min or better; corrected fund recomputed; reruns are idempotent.

poc.name: Borsa contract capture + Verda files
poc.measure: Land 9M contracts/day raw; cleanse; produce per-market files twice a day with manifest and hash.
poc.accept: No lost day (5-day source retention); files byte-identical to the current output on a test day.

poc.name: SPK report reconciliation
poc.measure: Build 3 of the 13 SPK reports from NOMX + Replica BIDB after the gün sonu event.
poc.accept: 100% reconciliation with the current Kale tables for the same business date.

poc.name: Replay and backfill
poc.measure: Replay a failed day from landing under a new load_id; backfill one year of positions.
poc.accept: Same result as the original run; no manual data fixes.

poc.name: Restart after failure
poc.accept: Restarts from the failed step without duplicates; operator steps documented in a runbook.

poc.name: Lineage
poc.measure: Trace one SPK report column back to source columns.
poc.accept: Column-level lineage available without manual spreadsheets.

poc.name: Automic + gün sonu event
poc.measure: Trigger the S2 chain from the batch-control record, not a clock.
poc.accept: Chain starts on the event; failures alert Automic and the owner.

poc.name: Security
poc.measure: Secrets handling, least-privilege accounts, TDE/VPD/redaction respected, audit of reads/exports.
poc.accept: Security team sign-off; no data or metadata leaves the bank.

poc.name: Promotion and CI
poc.measure: Promote a change DEV -> TEST -> PREPROD with automated tests.
